issue: Does 18 U.S.C. § 1505 reach obstruction of an agency proceeding that involves enforcement rather than adjudicative or rulemaking authority, such as ICE enforcement against noncitizens?

sides.position: Section 1505 is limited to agencies exercising adjudicative or rulemaking authority; ICE enforcement activity does not qualify as a pending proceeding.
cases: United States v. Hernandez, No. 24-4665 (4th Cir. 2026)

sides.position: Section 1505 applies to any pending proceeding before an agency, including proceedings where the agency enforces an order, and is not limited to agencies with adjudicative or rulemaking power.
cases: United States v. Kirst, 54 F.4th 605 (cited as 54 F.4th at 620)
United States v. Hopper, 177 F.3d 824 (cited as 177 F.3d at 828–31)
United States v. Senffner, 280 F.3d 757 (cited as 280 F.3d at 760–61)

this_court: The majority adopts the narrow reading, limiting § 1505 to agencies with adjudicative or rulemaking authority.
quote: Worse still, it does so without even giving these courts the respect to acknowledge the circuit split it has made.
cite: United States v. Dennis Hernandez, No. 24-4665 (4th Cir. 2026)
